sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of judicial discretion during supervised release revocations. the side that brought the case argues that specific statutory factors limit what judges can consider. The government contends that judges retain broad discretion to weigh any relevant considerations. The core conflict involves the interpretation of Section 3583(e) versus general sentencing principles.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the boundaries of judicial power in post-conviction supervision. It determines whether judges can punish based on the gravity of the original crime. The outcome shapes how courts balance public safety against individual liberty during supervised release.
